config.title: Doctor Appointment in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How the 116117 four-week guarantee really works in Berlin, which specialties need a coded referral, where the open consultation hours are, and why the fastest route cannot promise you English.

items.q: How do I get a doctor appointment in Berlin?
items.a: There are five routes and they are not equal. You can ring a practice yourself, use the KV Berlin appointment service online at 116117-termine.de, ring **116117**, sit in a practice's open consultation hours, or use the 116117 doctor on call for something that cannot wait. The appointment service is the only one carrying a legal ceiling of **four weeks**, and for most specialists it only works if your referral carries a twelve-digit Vermittlungscode.

items.q: Is the four-week rule for specialist appointments in Berlin actually binding?
items.a: The KV Berlin appointment service states that the wait between your call and your appointment is at most four weeks. The same page excludes **Bagatell- und Routineuntersuchungen**, minor complaints and routine check-ups, from that promise. It also places you at a practice that has a free slot rather than one you choose, and it serves people registered in Berlin who are insured with a statutory fund.

items.q: Which specialists in Berlin do I need a referral for?
items.a: The appointment service places you **without any referral** for a general practitioner, an eye doctor, a gynaecologist, a children's and adolescents' doctor including the U check-ups, and a first psychotherapy consultation. Everything else, from dermatology to cardiology, needs an **Überweisung zur fachärztlichen Weiterbehandlung with a twelve-digit Vermittlungscode**. A referral without that code does not open the four-week ceiling.

items.q: How long is a German referral valid?
items.a: A Muster 6 referral is valid in the quarter it was issued and in the quarter after it. A slip written in the middle of September 2026 runs until **31 December 2026**, and one written on 2 October runs until the end of March 2027. If you are handed a referral in the last days of a quarter and the problem is not urgent, waiting a few days for the new quarter buys you considerably more time.

items.q: Can I ask for an English-speaking doctor through 116117?
items.a: No. The KV Berlin appointment service says plainly that treatment in a foreign language cannot be taken into account when it places you. The separate public practice search at **arztsuche.116117.de** is a different tool and does carry a **Fremdsprachen** filter with English in it, alongside filters for step-free access and the specialty. If language matters more than speed, search there and book the practice yourself.

items.q: What is an offene Sprechstunde and which Berlin practices have one?
items.a: It is open consultation time you can walk into with no appointment. Since the 2019 Terminservice- und Versorgungsgesetz a specialist practice with a full licence owes **five hours a week** of it. The duty covers eye medicine, surgery, gynaecology and obstetrics, ear nose and throat, skin, child and adolescent psychiatry, neurology, neurosurgery, psychiatry, orthopaedics and urology. Practices choose their own times and a smaller licence carries a smaller duty, so ring the practice and ask when theirs falls this week.

No. The appointment service places no dental or orthodontic appointments at all, and no referral changes that. For a dentist you contact practices yourself, and Berlin runs a separate dental on-call service for out-of-hours pain, which is not the same line as the 116117 doctor on call.

items.q: What happens if I cancel an appointment that 116117 arranged?
items.a: If you cancel, you have no claim to a replacement appointment. There is one exception: if you cancel with the practice **on the same day** you agreed the appointment, you may use the appointment service again. If you simply cannot attend, tell the practice early so the slot can go to someone else.

items.q: When should I call 112 instead of 116117 in Berlin?
items.a: **112** is for something life-threatening. **116117** is for something that cannot wait until practices open but is not an emergency, and it answers around the clock, seven days a week. Using the on-call doctor to jump a routine specialist queue does not work and takes the slot from someone who needs it that night.
